curriculum.title: Path
curriculum.blurb: Left is start. Right is the interview. Same-column units can be done in any order.

stages.label: Kernel
stages.blurb: Cost and layout before any pattern.

stages.label: Index
stages.blurb: Remember what you have seen. Scan from both ends.

stages.label: Window
stages.blurb: A live range, a waiting stack, two speeds.

stages.label: Runtime
stages.blurb: What the machine is doing while your loop runs.

stages.label: Graph
stages.blurb: Shape first, then walk, then order.

stages.label: Wire
stages.blurb: Packets, locks, and the lie isolation sells.

stages.label: Frame
stages.blurb: How to spend forty-five minutes, then the cheap building blocks.

stages.label: Box
stages.blurb: One job, one box. Lookup, flags, edge, money.

stages.label: Harness
stages.blurb: The loop you rent versus the loop you write.

stages.label: Judge
stages.blurb: Measure the agent, then sit the round.

lessons.title: Mistakes coding agents keep making
lessons.summary: Coding agents fail in a short list of ruts — skipping repro, editing the wrong file, looping tools, hallucinating APIs — and evals plus harness design should hunt those ruts by name.

company_signal.name: Meta
company_signal.evidence: Candidate reports of 2026 AI-assisted coding rounds score whether you verify the model's patch instead of pasting it.

company_signal.name: Anthropic
company_signal.evidence: Public coding-agent and eval writeups catalog tool loops, skipped repro, and prompt-only "fixes" as first-class failure modes.

lessons.title: Contiguous slots versus pointer chasing
lessons.summary: Arrays buy random access and cache lines; linked lists buy cheap splices if you already hold the node.

company_signal.name: Amazon
company_signal.evidence: OA and phone-screen writeups still mix array two-pointer prompts with "reverse a linked list" / cycle detection as default list warmups.

lessons.title: Expand level by level
lessons.summary: Use a queue to visit nodes in distance order so the first time you reach a node is the shortest unweighted path.

company_signal.name: Meta
company_signal.evidence: Candidate reports list grid BFS (islands, nearest gate, word ladder) as a common onsite coding prompt.

company_signal.name: Amazon
company_signal.evidence: OA and phone-screen writeups keep using shortest-path-in-a-warehouse-grid as a graph warmup.

lessons.title: Big-O as a conversation
lessons.summary: Big-O is how you name the bottleneck and compare plans, not a stopwatch reading.

company_signal.name: Google
company_signal.evidence: Phone-screen writeups still open with "what's the complexity" before a line of code lands; candidates report justifying O(n) vs O(n log n) out loud.

lessons.title: Binary search the feasible number
lessons.summary: Search the numeric answer, not the array index, by testing a monotonic feasibility predicate.

company_signal.name: Google

company_signal.name: Meta
company_signal.evidence: Tagged-list threads list koko-style eating / split-array variants as medium follow-ups after vanilla binary search.

company_signal.evidence: The 2026 agent-eval essay separates capability measurement from regression gates as different products of the same harness.

lessons.title: Fewest tokens for a fare
lessons.summary: Fill a one-dimensional table of fewest tokens for each amount so greedy mistakes cannot hide in a local choice.

lessons.title: Training modules with prereqs
lessons.summary: Peel directed modules with indegree zero until none remain; a leftover node is a cycle and the catalog is impossible.

company_signal.name: Google

lessons.title: Explore, undo, try the next branch
lessons.summary: Walk a decision tree depth-first, pushing a choice onto the path and popping it before the next try.

company_signal.name: Meta

company_signal.name: Google
company_signal.evidence: Phone-screen writeups describe word-search / combination-sum style DFS as a recurring medium.

lessons.title: A name is not an address
lessons.summary: DNS is a cached tree walk from a stub to an authoritative name, not a magic lookup of a hostname.

company_signal.name: Amazon
company_signal.evidence: Candidate-reported backend screens still open with "what happens after you type a hostname" and expect cache, TTL, and who is authoritative, not a cloud logo.

lessons.title: Reuse the last few answers
lessons.summary: When a subproblem depends on a prefix of the input, store one number per prefix instead of recomputing the tree.

company_signal.name: Amazon
company_signal.evidence: Candidate OA reports keep listing house-robber / climb-stairs / coin-change as the 1D DP cluster.

company_signal.name: Google
company_signal.evidence: Phone-screen writeups describe "min cost to reach n" style recurrences as a common medium.

lessons.title: Fill a grid of overlapping subproblems
lessons.summary: When the state needs two indices, fill a table in an order that only reads already-solved cells.

company_signal.name: Meta

lessons.title: Bytes are not characters
lessons.summary: Unicode assigns code points to characters; UTF-8 and UTF-16 encode those points as bytes. Length, truncation, and HTTP headers all lie if you mix the layers.

company_signal.name: Google
company_signal.evidence: Frontend and API screens still catch candidates on string length, emoji, and "why did this JSON filename break in transit."

lessons.title: Eval harness versus agent harness
lessons.summary: The agent harness is how a model acts; the eval harness is how you score those actions. Mixing them up makes interview answers and production metrics lie.

company_signal.name: Anthropic
company_signal.evidence: Public engineering essay "Demystifying evals for AI agents" (Jan 2026) defines both terms and is now a common citation in AI-platform interviews.

company_signal.name: OpenAI / coding-agent vendors
company_signal.evidence: Candidate reports and harness-benchmark writeups treat Claude Code, Codex, etc. as agent harnesses wrapping a model.

lessons.title: Two speeds, one list
lessons.summary: Move two pointers at different speeds to find a cycle, a midpoint, or the k-th node from the end without extra memory.

company_signal.name: Amazon
company_signal.evidence: Linked-list cycle and "middle of the list" variants show up constantly in candidate OA reports.

company_signal.name: Microsoft
company_signal.evidence: Tagged-list threads still treat tortoise-and-hare list questions as a phone-screen staple.

lessons.title: Shipping dark, flipping in production
lessons.summary: Switchyard evaluates flags from a local snapshot so a config change is a versioned publish, not a 2M QPS dependency.

company_signal.name: Stripe
company_signal.evidence: Candidate-reported loops treat feature-flag / config-evaluation systems as a recurring mid-level prompt.

company_signal.name: Meta
company_signal.evidence: Prep-site frequency and candidate reports on feed/product ramps mention percentage rollouts and kill switches as follow-ups.

lessons.title: Floats are scientific notation, not decimals
lessons.summary: IEEE-754 floats store a sign, a power of two, and a short mantissa; most decimals never land exactly, and money should not live there.

company_signal.name: Stripe
company_signal.evidence: Payments screens and take-homes still ding candidates who store currency in float or compare totals with `===`.

lessons.title: Code graders, model judges, and humans
lessons.summary: Prefer a code check on world state; use an LLM judge for fuzzy qualities you have calibrated; keep humans as the gold you sample against.

company_signal.name: Anthropic
company_signal.evidence: The 2026 agent-eval essay treats code, model, and human graders as the three workable scoring methods and ranks them by objectivity.

lessons.title: Hash maps as an index
lessons.summary: Trade linear scans for expected constant lookups by storing the fact you will need later.

company_signal.name: Meta
company_signal.evidence: Candidate reports treat complement-index and frequency-map problems as the default first phone-screen question.

company_signal.name: Amazon
company_signal.evidence: OA writeups repeatedly mention counting / grouping with maps before any graph question.

lessons.summary: A hash table is an array of buckets plus a function that turns keys into indexes; collisions and resizes are why we say expected O(1).

company_signal.name: Meta
company_signal.evidence: Pair-sum / frequency-map phone screens routinely follow up with "why is this O(n)?" and "what if every key collides?"

lessons.title: Keep only the interesting k
lessons.summary: Stream n items through a size-k heap so you never sort the whole input just to name the extremes.

company_signal.name: Meta

lessons.title: Start evals from real failures, not a synthetic pile
lessons.summary: A useful agent eval is a small set of fully specified, already-solved failures run in clean rooms and graded on world state, then read by a human.

company_signal.name: OpenAI

lessons.title: HTTP is a conversation, TCP is the pipe

company_signal.name: Amazon

lessons.title: Indexes are precomputed answers
lessons.summary: An index is extra storage that turns a scan into a seek; you pay for it on every write, and the wrong index is worse than none.

company_signal.name: Amazon
